overview: Argentina is the second-largest country in South America, after Brazil. Its capital and largest city is Buenos Aires. Argentina won independence from Spain in 1816. Spanish is the official language, and many Argentines have Spanish or Italian ancestors. The country is famous for tango, beef and football, and its men's team has won the World Cup three times, most recently in 2022.

geography.text: Argentina stretches thousands of kilometres from the tropics in the north to Tierra del Fuego near Antarctica. The Andes run along its western border with Chile and include Aconcagua, the highest mountain outside Asia. The centre is covered by the Pampas, vast flat grasslands used for farming and cattle, while Patagonia in the south is dry, windy and thinly populated.

history.text: Spanish settlers founded Buenos Aires in the 1500s. Argentina declared independence from Spain in 1816, and later millions of immigrants, mostly from Italy and Spain, came to farm its rich land. The 1900s brought the populist government of Juan Perón, military dictatorships, and defeat by Britain in the Falklands War of 1982, after which democracy returned.

events.title: Buenos Aires founded
events.text: Spanish settlers found Buenos Aires for the second, lasting time.

events.title: Military coup
events.text: A dictatorship begins; thousands of people are 'disappeared'.

events.title: Falklands War
events.text: Argentina invades the Falkland Islands and is defeated by Britain.

government.text: Argentina is a federal presidential republic of 23 provinces and the city of Buenos Aires. The President is elected every four years and is both head of state and head of government. Congress has two chambers, the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate.

economy.text: Argentina has rich farmland in the Pampas and is one of the world's biggest exporters of soybeans, beef, wheat and corn. It also has large reserves of lithium and shale oil and gas. The economy has gone through repeated crises, with very high inflation and debt defaults.

culture.text: Tango was born in the working-class neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires in the late 1800s and is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list. Argentines love asado, a slow barbecue, and drink mate, a herbal tea shared from a gourd. The writer Jorge Luis Borges is one of the great authors of the 1900s.

items.title: Tango
items.text: A dance and music born in Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

items.title: Mate
items.text: A bitter herbal tea, sipped through a metal straw and passed around.

items.title: Iguazú Falls
items.text: Hundreds of waterfalls on the border with Brazil.

sport.text: Football is a passion in Argentina. The men's team has won the World Cup three times, most recently in 2022 led by Lionel Messi, and Diego Maradona is a national hero. Argentina is also strong in polo, rugby and basketball.

items.title: Lionel Messi
items.text: Won the Ballon d'Or a record eight times.

items.title: Polo
items.text: Argentina dominates the sport; the Argentine Open is played every year in Buenos Aires.

didYouKnow: Argentina has the highest mountain outside Asia, Aconcagua, at 6,961 metres.
The ballpoint pen was patented in Argentina by László Bíró after he moved there from Hungary.

keyPeople.name: Lionel Messi
keyPeople.text: Won the 2022 World Cup and eight Ballons d'Or.

keyPeople.name: Jorge Luis Borges
keyPeople.text: Famous for short stories about labyrinths and libraries.

keyPeople.name: Pope Francis
keyPeople.text: Born in Buenos Aires; led the Catholic Church from 2013 to 2025.
